comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The exact normalized target names English Language and Culture. Current official programme and adopted 2026–2027 EER confirm this specialization separately from American Studies. Retain the ordinary domestic pathway; do not substitute the conditional abroad/educational-minor replacement route. For the required 5-EC restricted choice, instantiate Adaptations: Page, Stage, Screen; for the 10-EC thesis choose English literature, the first listed thesis option. The 30-EC Arts-minor and 30-EC free-elective allocations remain genuine choice space, with their binding restrictions explicit. The restricted elective follows the first English-specialization-coded course in the adopted choice order (after the two American-Studies-coded entries); its selection does not depend on the UCR match.

progressionAssessment.rationale: All exact workbook terms and formal prerequisites pass. Literary introduction and stylistics precede advanced literary research; rhetoric precedes its practice module; film introduction precedes documentary and adaptation; introductory sociology precedes Modern Sociology; modern history precedes the source-based seminar. Level-three Philosophy of Emotion has no formal prerequisite and is placed in the final semester.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One coherent related-fields response materially addresses literary interpretation, linguistic stylistics, cultural production and representation, with 6 literature, 4 communication, 5 media and 5 history courses; it is not merely general humanities breadth. Literature/culture is already substantively covered and gives no second distinct concept. The first additional structural/historical/global English-linguistics direction was tested against Style & Meaning (actual syntax, semantics, discourse, pragmatics and cognition) and Psycholinguistics (acquisition, bilingualism, speech processing and hands-on experiments), brain/behaviour foundations and research methods. These are positive contributions, but cannot supply a coherent 24-course response to English structure, variation, phonology and historical development; generic psychology or computing substitutions would change its defining subject. Advanced proficiency lacks a dedicated development sequence despite genuine rhetorical, academic and creative writing. Science/politics/business describes English-language use, not three curricular specializations. Teaching was tested through primary-school rhetorical teaching, Psycholinguistics, brain/behaviour and Lifespan Developmental Psychology; these do not establish an English-learning/secondary pedagogy programme. Rejection is substantive, not the lack of a teaching licence. Stop after the first failed additional concept; subsequent retained tests document coverage, not a third alternative.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both directly teach literary interpretation and critical reading; the UCR introduction covers more than English literature.
Both study adaptation of literary texts across media. UCR concentrates on text-to-film analysis and adaptation theory; the selected external elective also includes stage adaptation.

Both support research in literary studies. UCR applies critical perspectives in a textual research project; it does not cover the seminar’s full English-language-and-culture scope or replace the bachelor’s thesis.

Both address linguistic description and analysis. UCR applies grammar, semantics, discourse and cognition to textual interpretation; this is a substantive part of introductory language analysis, not a complete general linguistics curriculum.
Both develop oral communication; UCR focuses on rhetorical argument rather than English-language proficiency.
The UCR course directly studies American popular-media narratives and social life, one important part of the British/American component; it does not supply British popular-culture coverage.

Both develop academic writing and presentation. UCR teaches scholarly-source evaluation, literature synthesis and research introductions alongside reflective and civic work; it does not reproduce English-specific proficiency assessment.

The selected programme develops scholarly and creative writing, but no course provides the dedicated English-language development of Writing English. PPD is placed with Academic Communication Skills, its stronger specific educational function.

Modern History and History of Empires provide comparative historical interpretation, not the sustained British-history subject of this component; the current history research seminar supplies no verified British case.
No selected course teaches the English speech-sound/pronunciation training that defines this component.
Philosophy of Emotion contributes focused emotion and art theory; that narrower topic does not establish the primary philosophy-of-culture content of this component.
World literary comparison, life narratives and American media history contribute related methods and cultural subjects, but none establishes a sustained survey of American literature.

Style & Meaning substantively applies syntax within wider stylistic analysis and is placed with Introduction to Linguistics. No other selected course independently supplies this English syntax component; it is not duplicated across rows.
No selected course provides the historical development of English; comparative imperial history is not historical linguistics.
Great Literary Works offers world-literary comparison and modernist interpretation rather than a sustained nineteenth-/twentieth-century British literary-period survey.
The selected literary courses teach genre, interpretation and critical approaches, not a sustained seventeenth-/eighteenth-century British literary survey.
History of Empires supplies historical context, but no selected course directly studies the global linguistic spread and varieties of English.
No selected course supplies the systematic phonological study of English; poetic sound and rhetorical delivery do not establish that linguistic content.
No selected course provides Middle English literature in its historical-language and literary setting; comparative myth is not a substitute.

No selected course supplies second-language-acquisition research. Psycholinguistics has genuine acquisition content but belongs to the separately assessed, rejected additional concept and is not scheduled here.

The literary curriculum includes drama and adaptation, but no selected course establishes sustained early-modern stage study; ancient tragedy and general film adaptation are different primary subjects.
PPD supports academic and personal development, but is already placed with academic communication. No selected course independently supplies English/American Studies-specific career orientation.
The required 10-EC English-literature thesis remains distinct from course research projects. UCR optional independent research is displayed separately in this row, outside the scheduled180EC.

notes.text: Radboud combines advanced English proficiency, linguistics and sustained British and other Anglophone literary study with independent research. This UCR programme offers substantial literary, stylistic and cultural analysis through literature, rhetoric, media and history. Its grammar, discourse analysis and academic writing are meaningful contributions, while dedicated English-proficiency development, phonetics, phonology, historical-English study and the full British literary-period sequence remain gaps.

audience.programmeDescription: Explore English language, literature and culture through language development, linguistics, British and other English-speaking literary traditions, and independent research. The English Language and Culture track is distinct from American Studies.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This UCR programme offers sustained literary interpretation, linguistic stylistics, creative expression, film and cultural history. These subjects respond to important parts of English Studies. Its language analysis and academic writing provide partial correspondences; it does not reproduce the dedicated English-proficiency, structural and historical linguistics curriculum or the full British literary-period sequence.
